title: Optimized protocol for in vivo affinity purification proteomics and biochemistry using C. elegans
protocol: Design transgenic constructs to express tagged POI and tagged control for affinity purification.
Test all genetic constructs with phenotypic assays to ensure that the tagged-POI is functional.
Clone expression constructs containing the native gene promoter, gene (cDNA or ORF), and native 3′ UTR.
Microinject POI protein null mutants (P0) with plasmids containing transgene and co-injection markers.
Select transgenic strains with 40%–60% transmission of the co-injection marker.
Test strains isolated in step 2.c for expression and function of the affinity tagged POI using phenotypic rescue experiments.
Return to step 2.b and adjust injection concentrations if necessary.
Alter the location of the tag on the POI or test different linkers in step 1.a if needed.
Biochemically test transgenic strains isolated for affinity tagged-POI.
Mix 20 μL of 1 mg/mL TMP with 380 μL of M9.
Add the TMP solution to a tube containing 200 late L4 extrachromosomal array-carrying worms in 200 μL of M9.
Incubate at 20°C–23°C for 15 min on a rotator with gentle mixing.
Transfer TMP treated worms to an unseeded 10 cm NGM plate in the dark.
Expose worms to 350 μJ/cm3 UV using Spectroline UV crosslinker.
Add concentrated OP50 after UV exposure and let worms recover at 15°C.
Pick 10 healthy young adult transgenics (P0s) to 10 plates each the next day.
Pick 25 F1 plates from each P0 plate for the next generation.
Pick 3–5 F2s from each F1 plate and transfer them to individual plates in the following generation.
Screen F2s for 100% transmission of transgenic array integration into the genome.
Outcross transgenic integrants at least four times.
Cross integrated transgene onto POI null mutant (preferably protein null).
Secondary check for rescue by confirming affinity tagged POI expression through immunoprecipitation and western blot.
Set up the liquid culture when Day 1 plates are fully starved.
Prepare 500 mL of S Complete media using sterile procedures on the same day.
Add 225 mL of S Complete to each of the 2 × 2 L flasks.
Add 5 mL of prepared liquid HB101 culture to each flask.
Transfer worms from Day 1 plate into a 15 mL conical tube.
Pour M9 onto the plate, swirl and remove liquid using a glass pipette and add to the conical tube.
Wash worms three times: for each wash, add 10 mL of M9, spin worms down at 350 × g for 1 min 30 s, aspirate supernatant and repeat.
After the final wash, resuspend worms in 6 mL of M9.
Divide resuspended worms equally (3 mL) into two Erlenmeyer flasks prepared above.
Place flasks on an orbital shaker and set at 185 RPM with a 2-inch orbit at 20°C–23°C.
Harvest Day 2 plates by washing with M9 as described in step 6d.
Divide the resuspended worms equally between the flasks set up at step 6e.
Feed by adding 7.5 mL of HB101 to each flask.
On the 3rd day of culture, add 10 mL of liquid HB101 culture to each flask for additional food.
After 24 hours (day 4 of culture), check health and density of worms.
Pipette 1 mL of liquid culture onto an unseeded NGM plate.
Let the liquid evaporate and observe the worms’ health and density.
Note that some HB101 bacteria should still be present, indicating sufficient food.
Observe visible gut granules in worms to confirm good health.
Harvest liquid cultures by spinning cultures from one flask into a 250 mL conical tube.
Prepare a C. elegans-sucrose mixture with a 2 mL layer of NaCl for separation during sucrose flotation.
Distribute liquid culture from the two flasks into 10 × 50 mL conical tubes or 2 × 250 mL conical bottles.
Put tubes on ice to let worms settle for 5 min.
Spin worms down at 750 × g, 4 min at 20°C–23°C.
Aspirate off supernatant with a vacuum leaving 5 ml of liquid on top of the worm pellet.
Consolidate the worms into two 50 mL conical tubes.
Adjust volume to 50 mL with 0.1 M NaCl and mix by inverting.
Spin down at 750 × g, 4 min.
Aspirate supernatant leaving 10 mL of liquid on top of the worm pellet.
Resuspend worm pellet and transfer into 4 × 15 mL tubes.
Adjust volume to 6 mL of worms per tube using 0.1 M NaCl.
Add 6 mL of ice-cold sterile 60% sucrose to each tube of worms.
Mix tubes well by inverting several times.
Overlay the suspension with 2 mL of 0.1 M NaCl using a 5 mL glass pipet.
Spin the tubes (1,450 × g, 2 min 30 s) with no or minimal deceleration.
Collect worms in NaCl using a glass pipette carefully to avoid sucrose layer contamination.
Deposit collected worms into 15 mL tubes containing 10 mL of NaCl prepared previously.
Mix the tubes well by inverting several times.
Spin the tubes (350 × g, 1 min 30 s) and aspirate supernatant.
Wash the tubes two times to remove sucrose: add 15 mL 0.1 M NaCl, spin down (350 × g, 1 min 30 s), and aspirate the supernatant.
After final wash, leave a small amount (<200 μL) of liquid over the worm pellet for resuspension.
Resuspend worms in prechilled ceramic mortar with liquid N2 to 75% full using pipette pump and Pasteur pipette.
Add slightly more 0.1 M NaCl if necessary to facilitate pipetting.
Transfer a small drop of clean animals to an unseeded NGM plate to assess sample quality.
Pipette resuspended worms dropwise into liquid N2 and flash freeze into small beads.
Pour frozen worm beads into a prechilled 50 mL conical tube.
Measure the mass of beads after liquid N2 has fully evaporated.
Store frozen worms at -80°C.
Prechill all conical tubes on dry ice and metal spatulas in liquid N2.
Measure 5 g of worm pellets per strain into prechilled 50 mL conical tubes and keep on dry ice.
Add a half of a Roche cOmplete mini protease inhibitor cocktail EDTA free tablet to each tube.
Assemble the cryomill, grinding jar, and grinding ball according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Run pre-cool setting for 5 min to cool jars with liquid N2.
Pour contents of conical tube into the grinding jar with grinding ball.
Pre-cool the jar for 2 min at 5 Hz, then grind for 5 min at 30 Hz.
Remove ground worms from jar using liquid N2 and prechilled mortar.
Use prechilled metal spatula to remove any grindate stuck to jar wall and grinding ball.
Pour ground worms and liquid N2 mix into the prechilled conical tube.
Let liquid N2 evaporate and return the tube to dry ice.
Clean work surfaces with 70% isopropanol before each experiment.
Use gloves, surgical mask, hair net, and lab coat while handling samples.
Wash high-speed centrifuge tubes, cryomill grinding jars, and balls with Contrad 70 detergent.
Dry washed items using filtered 70% isopropanol with low particulate cleanroom pads.
Remove C. elegans grindates stored at -80°C from the freezer.
Tap tube to dislodge aggregates or use a sterile spatula to loosen them quickly.
Add room temperature lysis buffer in a 1:4 w/v ratio to ground worms (e.g., resuspend 5 g worms in 20 mL lysis buffer).
Mix worm lysate with a sterile plastic spatula for less than 1 minute.
Incubate the mixture on a rotator for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer lysates to prechilled centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge lysates at 20,000 × g for 10–15 minutes at 4°C.
Pipette supernatant into prechilled 50 mL conical tube.
Do not freeze lysate after this step. Keep on ice.
Perform BCA assay following manufacturer’s instructions to assess total protein concentration in lysate.
Calculate amount of lysate needed for 80 mg total protein.
Prepare 2 × 250 μL of Dynabeads (10 mg/mL stock) in 2 × 15 mL tubes by washing with cold lysis buffer 3 times.
Collect beads with a DynaMag-15 magnet and discard the supernatant using a serological pipet after each wash.
Transfer volume of lysate equivalent to 40 mg of total protein (about 10 mL) to each 15 mL conical tube of Dynabeads for a total of 80 mg total protein.
Incubate with rotation at 4°C for 1–4 h.
Use the DynaMag-15 magnet to collect Dynabeads for 2 minutes.
Invert the tube twice while on the magnet to collect any Dynabeads in the tube cap.
Add 8 mL of cold lysis buffer to the tube, remove the magnet, and invert several times.
Collect beads with a DynaMag-15 magnet and discard the supernatant using a serological pipet after each wash.
Repeat washes  five times.
Transfer the beads to a 1.7 mL low retention tube.
Add 500 μL of cold lysis buffer to the Dynabeads and gently resuspend.
Transfer 50 μL (10%) of suspension to a new tube, collect the beads using DynaMag-2, and aspirate supernatant.
Set samples aside for quality control analysis.
Collect beads from the remaining 450 μL (90%) resuspension using the DynaMag-2 and aspirate supernatant.
Store beads at −80°C until ready to perform mass spectrometry.
Add 25 μL of 1× LDS sample buffer directly to Dynabeads for quality control.
Heat samples at 70°C for 10 minutes.
Agitate tubes by flicking halfway through incubation to mix beads.
Collect the beads with a DynaMag-2 magnet to separate them from the supernatant.
Use the supernatant for silver staining and western blotting.
Place NuPAGE gel into an Invitrogen running apparatus.
Add appropriate buffer according to manufacturer’s recommendations.
Reconstitute human recombinant POI under 150 kDa using a 4%–12% Bis-Tris gel.
Load 90% of the diagnostic sample into NuPAGE gel.
Load protein molecular weight standards alongside samples for analysis.
Run NuPAGE gel according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Perform silver staining using Pierce silver stain kit, following manufacturer’s instructions.
Determine the quality of affinity purification by comparing bands in POI sample with negative control sample.
Prepare a Western blot to confirm expression of POI.
Load 10% of the diagnostic sample into a NuPAGE gel and run.
Transfer gel to PVDF membrane using wet transfer in TAC buffer at 4°C.
Block PVDF membrane with 5% milk in TBS-T for 1 hour at 20°C–23°C.
Incubate blot in primary antibody diluted in 5% milk and TBS-T for 16–20 hours at 4°C.
Wash blot with TBS-T three times for 5 minutes each.
Incubate blot in secondary antibody diluted in TBS-T for 1 hour at 20°C–23°C.
Wash blot with TBS-T three times and then with TBS three times.
Incubate blot with chemiluminescent substrate (SuperSignal West Pico/Femto).
Develop using x-ray film or digital bioimager (Azure).
Prepare sample for MS by adding 50 μL of Laemmli sample buffer to frozen Dynabeads from step 17.r (90% of total purified sample).
Boil samples at 95°C for 15 minutes.
Run boiled samples on Mini-Protean TGX Tris-Glycine Precast Gel (Biorad) at 120 V for 10 minutes until entire sample just enters top of gel.
Coomassie stain gel at 20°C–23°C for 1 hour with shaking.
De-stain the gel to reveal protein samples.
Excise compressed gel bands containing entire sample using a new razor blade and individual Eppendorf tube for each test strain and control.
Treat excised gel pieces with 10 mM DTT.
Treat with 50 mM iodoacetamide.
In-gel digest sample with 60 ng/μL trypsin, adding enough volume to cover gel pieces.
Acidify and desalt peptide pools using a Zip-Tip C18 column (5 μg capacity).
Resuspend samples in 0.1% formic acid.
Perform liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS).
Load sample into EASY-nLC 1000 system coupled to Nanospray Flex Ion Source and Orbitrap Fusion (or Lumos) Tribrid Mass Spectrometer.

Elute peptides in analytical RP column (0.075 × 150 mm Acclaim PepMap RLSC nano Viper) operated at 300 nL/min using the following gradient: 2%–25% solvent B for 40 minutes, 25%–44% solvent B for 20 minutes, 44%–80% solvent B for 10 seconds, 80% solvent B for 5 minutes, 80-5% solvent B for 10 seconds, and 5% solvent B for 20 minutes.
Compare outcomes for a given candidate with different extraction conditions.
Calculate normalized total spectral count for the candidate protein based on its size and the number of peptides identified for the protein of interest by MS.
Design construct for tagged candidate protein using a distinct tag from POI.
Generate transgenic or CRISPR-engineered worms expressing tagged candidate protein.
Perform co-IP (or other interaction assay) to verify physical interaction between candidate and POI.
Use 1 to 10 mg of total protein from whole worm extracts for the assay.
Use 10–15 μL of protein G agarose beads coupled to appropriate primary antibody to immunoprecipitate tagged POI protein complexes.
Evaluate if a single mutant for candidate phenocopies the mutant for POI.
Generate and test a strain with null mutations in both candidate and POI to examine genetic interactions.
Test for colocalization between POI and proteomic candidates.
Engineer different fluorescent tags onto the POI and candidate using transgenics or CRISPR engineering.
Evaluate colocalization with confocal microscopy or other high-resolution microscopy techniques.
Generate RPM-1 transgenic worms using a native rpm-1 promoter.
Express GS::RPM-1 in the nervous system using genomic DNA on an rpm-1 protein null mutant background.
Introduce point mutations to create GS::RPM-1 ligase dead (LD) for biochemical 'trap' function.
Express GS-tagged GFP (GS::GFP) as a control strain under the same conditions.
Conduct microinjections on a pha-1(e2123); rpm-1(ju44) protein null mutant background using a concentration of RPM-1 plasmid previously shown to rescue mutant phenotypes and a PHA-1 rescue cassette.
Use PHA-1 positive selection for facilitating biochemical screening for GS::RPM-1 transgenic lines.
Maintain non-transgenic pha-1; rpm-1 mutants at 23°C to arrest them at the L1 larval stage.
Ensure only transgenic worms are present in large-scale liquid cultures by using PHA-1 selection.
Test functionality of GS tagged RPM-1 through phenotypic rescue.
Integrate extrachromosomal arrays.
Test expression of GS::RPM-1, GS::RPM-1 LD, and GS::GFP control using western blot.
Integrate one extrachromosomal array for each construct into the genome using the TMP/UV protocol.
Outcross integrants to a wild-type background.
Isolate integrants on an rpm-1(ju44) protein null mutant background.
Evaluate rescue of integrants with integrated GS::RPM-1.
Perform affinity purifications from integrated transgenic strains using IgG coupled Dynabeads.
Conduct quality control diagnostics by silver staining for sample analysis.
Carry out Western blotting to confirm the presence of purified POIs, GS::RPM-1 and GS::RPM-1 LD.
Analyze RPM-1 AP-proteomics results.
Use Scaffold (Proteome Software) to validate peptides and protein identifications detected by LC-MS/MS.
Assess RPM-1 binding proteins using the criteria described above in step 23.
Remove ribosomal proteins as they are involved in translation.
Exclude vitellogenins due to their role in post-embryonic development.
Eliminate keratin as it is a contaminant from sample preparation.
Remove GFP since it is present only in the negative control.
POI amount because the GS::RPM-1 level is consistently lower than GS::RPM-1 LD.
Consider protein size of proteomics candidates since larger proteins are more likely to be identified.
